title_original: Patrick Stewart’s Career in Photos: ‘Star Trek,’ ‘X-Men,’ ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ and More

blocks.text: Patrick Stewart, who died Wednesday at 86 , starred in dozens of film, shows and TV movies across 60 years on screen. He was best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard on “Star Trek” and Prof. Charles Xavier in the “X-Men” movies, and he received four Emmy nominations, three Golden Globe noms, a Tony nod and one Grammy win during his career.

“His professional accomplishments were humbly matched by his philanthropy and activism on behalf of human rights, survivors of domestic violence, global refugees, veterans’ mental health services, and animal welfare, particularly his cherished foster pitties,” a statement on his Instagram read. “He was a Knight, Chancellor, motor sport enthusiast, and lifelong Huddersfield Football fan. He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life.”
Stewart’s “Star Trek” and Marvel co-stars have shared tributes to him online, in addition to his countless fans.

“Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor,” wrote fellow “Star Trek” icon William Shatner. “From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work. My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed.”
Revisit Stewart’s career in photos below.

Dune (1984) Image Credit: ©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection In David Lynch’s 1984 version of “Dune,” Stewart played Gurney Halleck, a troubador-warrior and baliset musician in the Atreides court, co-starring with Kyle MacLachlan and Max Von Sydow.

blocks.alt: DUNE, Max Von Sydow (standing front), Patrick Stewart (standing center), Kyle MacLachlan (seated), Jurgen Prochnow (standing right), 1984, © Universal/courtesy Everett Collection
blocks.caption: Image Credit: ©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection

blocks.text: Star Trek: The Next Generation (1987) Image Credit: ©Paramount/Courtesy Everett Col Stewart debuted as Captain Jean-Luc Picard, the commanding officer of the Federation starship USS Enterprise, when “Star Trek: The Next Generation” aired on September 28, 1987.

blocks.alt: STAR TREK: THE NEXT GENERATION, 1987-94, Patrick Stewart, Jonathan Frakes, Brent Spiner, in the 3rd Season cliffhanger finale episode, Best of Both Worlds-Pt.1 5/18/90- Ep#174. Paramount/Courtesy: Everett Collection.
blocks.caption: Image Credit: ©Paramount/Courtesy Everett Col

blocks.text: Star Trek: Generations (1994) Stewart reprised his role as Picard on the big screen in “Star Trek: Generations” on November 18, 1994. He starred in later “Star Trek” movies like “First Contact” (1996), “Insurrection” (1998) and “Nemesis” (2002).

Moby Dick (1998) Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection As Captain Ahab, Stewart hunted down the great white whale that had bitten off his leg years prior in this TV mini-series adaptation of Herman Melville’s novel. He was nominated for an Emmy for the role.

blocks.alt: MOBY DICK, Patrick Stewart, 1998 TV Movie
blocks.caption: Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection

blocks.text: Safe House (1998) Image Credit: ©Showtime Networks Inc./Courtes Stewart played Mace Sowell, a retired DIA agent that has incriminating evidence on his former boss who’s now running for president. The TV film aired in the UK in late 1998 and in the U.S. in January 1999.

blocks.alt: SAFE HOUSE, (from left): Patrick Stewart, Kimberly Williams, 1998. © Showtime / Courtesy: Everett Collection
blocks.caption: Image Credit: ©Showtime Networks Inc./Courtes

blocks.text: A Christmas Carol (1999) Image Credit: ©Hallmark Entertainment/Courtes As Ebenezer Scrooge, Stewart was visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come in this holiday TV movie.

blocks.alt: A CHRISTMAS CAROL, Patrick Stewart, 1999. (c)Hallmark Entertainment/ Courtesy: Everett Collection.
blocks.caption: Image Credit: ©Hallmark Entertainment/Courtes

blocks.text: X-Men (2000) Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett C Stewart debuted as Prof. Charles Xavier, the leader of the X-Men mutant team, in the 2000 film. His powerful telekinetic mutant mentored young heroes and clashed with his old friend and rival Magneto (Ian McKellen). He also appeared in sequels and spinoffs like “X2” (2003), “The Last Stand” (2006), “X-Men Origins: Wolverine” (2009), “The Wolverine” (2013) and “Days of Future Past” (2014).

blocks.alt: X-MEN, Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, 2000, TM and copyright (c) 20th Century Fox Film Corp. All rights reserved
blocks.caption: Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett C

blocks.text: King of Texas (2002) Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection This TV film reinvented Shakespeare’s “King Lear” and set the tale in the Republic of Texas during the 19th century. Stewart starred as John Lear, a wealthy cattle baron who divided his land amongst his daughters.

The Lion in Winter (2003) Image Credit: ©Showtime Networks Inc./Courtes Stewart played King Henry II in this TV film, which co-starred Glenn Close as Eleanor of Aquitaine. He was nominated for a Golden Globe for his role in this TV movie remake of the Peter O’Toole classic.

blocks.alt: THE LION IN WINTER, Glenn Close, Patrick Stewart, 2003, © SHOWTIME / Courtesy: Everett Collection
blocks.caption: Image Credit: ©Showtime Networks Inc./Courtes

blocks.text: Green Room (2015) Image Credit: Everett Collection / Everett Collection In Jeremy Saulnier’s thriller, Stewart plays the bar owner and leader of a Nazi group who attack a punk band that has just witnessed a murder in the Pacific Northwest.

blocks.alt: GREEN ROOM, from left: Brent Werzner, Colton Ruscheinsky, Patrick Stewart, Mason Knight, Samuel Summer, 2015. ph: Scott Patrick Green/ © A24 /courtesy Everett Collection
blocks.caption: Image Credit: Everett Collection / Everett Collection

blocks.text: Blunt Talk (2015) Image Credit: ©Starz! Movie Channel/Courtesy In this Starz series, Stewart played Walter Blunt, a military veteran and turned cable journalist, and received another Golden Globe nomination.

blocks.alt: BLUNT TALK, Patrick Stewart, 'The Queen of Hearts', (Season 1, ep. 105, airs Sept. 19, 2015). photo: Justina Mintz / © Starz / Courtesy: Everett Collection
blocks.caption: Image Credit: ©Starz! Movie Channel/Courtesy

blocks.text: Logan (2017) Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection Stewart and Hugh Jackman reunited as Xavier and Wolverine in “Logan,” the first R-rated “X-Men” spinoff. In the future-set spinoff, Xavier suffered from a degenerative disease and accidentally killed many mutants, and his character dies in the film alongside Wolverine.

blocks.alt: LOGAN, l-r: Patrick Stewart, Hugh Jackman, 2017. ph: Ben Rothstein/TM & copyright © 20th Century Fox Film Corp. All rights reserved./courtesy Everett Collection
blocks.caption: Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection

blocks.text: Avengers: Doomsday (2026) In what may be his final on-screen appearance, Stewart will return as Xavier in “Avengers: Doomsday” on Dec. 18. It will mark the first time that the Avengers, X-Men, Fantastic Four and more heroes will all cross over in the MCU.
